claims.text: A 60-second apnea window from recording a01, starting at 2000-01-01T03:42:00+00:00 and ending at 03:43:00+00:00, was flagged as an anomaly by the detector.

The detector classified the window as an anomaly with a reconstruction error of 0.3607, exceeding the anomaly threshold of 0.0453 by a normalized margin of 6.9644; this is reconstruction threshold evidence, not a probability or calibrated confidence.
The model is a BiLSTM temporal-attention autoencoder (version apnea-01-a01_seed2026) trained on the apnea dataset, with test patient a01 and fold ID apnea-01-a01.
The signal summary for the window includes 6000 samples from the primary ECG channel at 100 Hz, with additional derived channels (mean, std, min, max, range, slope, energy) available.

Temporal attention for the window peaked at 2000-01-01T03:42:19.200000+00:00 with a maximum value of 0.0115 and mean 0.0100; this represents shared window-level temporal relevance, not probability, calibrated confidence, or channel-specific importance.

The current event is an anomaly detection in a 60-second apnea window from recording a01, supported by reconstruction error above threshold and temporal attention peaking early in the window; no longitudinal PDM context or clinical context was supplied in this evidence package.
